topic: Helios: Open-Source AI Agent Observability with Tracing and Cost Monitoring

competitors.name: Langfuse
key_points: Open source LLM engineering platform with observability, evals, prompt management, playground, datasets
Strong trace store but teams own more of the agent-specific evaluation layer themselves
Best for teams wanting open-source LLM tracing with eval layer built on top

competitors.name: Arize Phoenix
key_points: AI Observability & Evaluation platform with OpenTelemetry compatibility
Open-source entry point for OTel-compatible traces
Arize AX adds hosted dashboards, retention, and evaluation workflows
Best for teams wanting OpenTelemetry-compatible tracing plus custom evaluators

competitors.name: OpenLLMetry (Traceloop)
key_points: Open-source observability for GenAI/LLM applications based on OpenTelemetry
Lightweight integration with existing OTel infrastructure

competitors.name: Helicone
key_points: Open source LLM observability platform — one line of code to monitor, evaluate, and experiment
Caching layer improves speed and reduces costs

competitors.name: AgentOps
key_points: Python SDK for AI agent monitoring, LLM cost tracking, benchmarking
Integrates with CrewAI, Agno, OpenAI Agents SDK, Langchain, Autogen, AG2, CamelAI
Focus on agent-specific monitoring rather than general LLM observability

stats.fact: Agentic AI market projected to grow from $7.6B to $236B by 2034 (40%+ CAGR)
88% of AI agents fail to reach production
AI agents that reach production deliver an average 171% ROI (192% in the US)
79% of enterprises have adopted AI agents in some form, but only 11% run them in production
MCP (Model Context Protocol) reached 97 million downloads within months of release with 1,000+ servers
Langfuse leads open-source LLM observability with 31,857 GitHub stars
Arize Phoenix has 10,733 GitHub stars as the leading AI observability platform
OpenLLMetry (Traceloop) has 7,328 GitHub stars for OTel-based GenAI observability
Helios is a brand-new project (created July 22, 2026) with 1 GitHub star, MIT licensed

angles: Helios uniquely combines tracing, cost analytics, AND security monitoring (PII detection, prompt injection detection) in a single open-source platform — most competitors focus on tracing/cost only
Built-in risk scoring engine that combines multiple detector signals into a per-run risk score — a differentiator from pure tracing tools
Async architecture: fast synchronous ingestion with async analysis pipeline (cost calculation, security scanning) keeps SDK calls fast
Self-hostable with single docker compose up — no vendor lock-in, full data ownership
Very early stage project (1 star, created 4 days ago) — opportunity to track its evolution from foundation to production-ready
The 88% agent failure rate makes observability infrastructure the critical missing piece — Helios addresses this gap specifically for agent workloads
Python SDK designed for <10 lines of code integration — drop-in instrumentation for existing agents
